text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for its accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The acute hard currency shortage on the interbank market boosted the demand for hard currency at retail shops, triggering a strong depreciation of the leu.
ADEVARUL
- The over-the-counter market is still in its infancy with only a handful of the 120 listed stocks involved in trading.
- Around 250,000 tonnes of imported crude oil are expected to reach the Black Sea port of Constanta this week. The amount is enough to meet the needs of refineries for one week.
- The underground economy accounts for 40 percent of Romania's gross domestic product.
LIBERTATEA
- The National Oil Company says it got $21 million financing from the Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA for oil imports.
- Economic stabilisation depends on financial discipline and control of payments arrears, central bank chief economist Daniel Daianu said during a banking seminar.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Small and medium-sized enterprises need laws which should encourage investment, was the conclusion of a management forum.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Prosecutors completed file against Greater Romania Party leader Corneliu Vadim Tudor accused of slandering 177 personalities. Prosecutors can ask newly elected upper Senate house to lift Tudor's parliamentary immunity.
- Vasile Bostan, chairman of the administration board at private Columna SA bank was elected vice-president of the Socialist Party.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The governing programme of the new cabinet led by Prime Minister-designate Victor Ciorbea will be presented on Saturday to a team of International Monetary Fund experts.
- Newspaper prints unofficial results of Saturday's talks between Democratic Convention (CDR), Social Democratic Union (USD) and Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) to form the new government.
- Newspaper says the UDMR will get the tourism portfolio.
- The USD is expected to get the foreign ministry and the environment, transports and justice portfolios, but no appointment was officially confirmed.
- The USD is also expected to appoint 13 of the 42 local prefects, the newspaper says.
- Local CDR organisation in the Transylvanian town of Oradea demanded that CDR mayor quit over failure to implement provisions of a 200-day "Contract with Oradea".
- A Romanian stowaway was found at Otopeni airport hiding in a Delta Airlines aircraft bound for Frankfurt.
ADEVARUL
- Romanian Catholic leaders to discuss in December inviting the Pope to visit the country.
- British ambassador to Bucharest, Christopher Crabbie, said in interview he would encourage British firms to prospect investment opportunities in Romania.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Prime minister-designate Victor Ciorbea said he would set up three new ministries: budget, public information and privatisation.
- Hungarian parliament to discuss ratification of the treaty with Romania on December 9. The treaty -- signed in September -- was already ratified by the Romanian parliament.
- Police investigations revealed that customs officers can earn some $200 per day in bribes.
- The UDMR wants to get the job of local prefect in the Transylvanian county of Covasna, mainly inhabited by ethnic Hungarians, newspaper says.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The Health Ministry to start campaign for vaccination of 600,000 14-year-olds against hepatitis B in March 1997.
- Romania's exiled former king Michael will not return soon, but "will wait for the right moment", Simina Mezincescu, the leader of monarchist organisation "Romania viitoare", said.
LIBERTATEA
- The Prime Minister will become "head of the council of ministers" in the new government.
ZIUA
- Actor Ion Caramitru who played a key role in the 1989 uprising could get the culture portfolio.
AZI
- Romania registered 315,000 abortions in the first eight months of 1996. More than 400,000 were registered last year.
- Radu Mazare, a journalist sentenced to seven months in jail for slander, was elected deputy of Constanta county. ($=3,508 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
